key_insight: Laser power, welding speed, and TIG current jointly control molten-pool flow, keyhole size, and arc stability in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel.
engineering_relevance: The findings provide process guidance for optimizing penetration, bead width, and arc behavior to improve weld quality in low-thermal-expansion Invar components.
method: Numerical simulation of molten-pool dynamics and heat transfer
High-speed photography of arc and pool behavior during welding
Parameter study across laser power, welding speed, and welding current
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that varying laser power (5–6 kW), welding speed (0.5–0.8 m/min), and current (150–170 A) measurably changed penetration depth, weld width, flow velocity, and arc deflection/stability.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on a limited process window and primarily describe single-parameter trends, so broader parameter coupling and material-thickness effects may require additional validation.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
